text:
olivia: Quick triage — Customer (FinPlatform) asked for a single "auto-optimize" surface: batching/caching/quant recommendations + eval-triggered alerts. Can we scope an MVP for Q3? @kevin @maya
kevin: we should split into 3 smaller pieces: recs (offline + UI), alerting tied to evals, and an infra-safe runtime suggestion API. each has different risk.
maya: +1. Customer wants actionable recs (e.g., quantize to int8/4, enable KV prefix cache, batch size suggestions) and a way to get alerted when evals regress after model swap.
sam: what's the acceptance criteria for "actionable"? we need reproducible perf/quality deltas and a rollback path.
jen: propose MVP scope: 1) recs engine (offline only) that outputs: model variant, quant profile, batch size recommendation with expected p95 latency & token cost delta; 2) eval alert plumbing (hook into eval jobs, threshold-based alerts); 3) UI table + export. no automatic quants/rollouts in MVP.
olivia: sounds good. tradeoffs: offline recs reduce risk but customers asked for near-real-time suggestions. can we promise weekly cadence for first release?
kevin: weekly is reasonable. we can run jobs against recent traffic traces to score recs. infra effort mainly around safe simulation (KV cache sim + batched latency model).
maya: for alerting we should support two modes: simple threshold + top-down regression buckets. example rule syntax suggestion:
```yaml
rule: eval_regression
trigger: "delta_metric(q_prompt, quality) <= -0.03"
window: 3 runs
action: notify=#cust-eng, create-ticket=OPT-422
```
kevin: +1. also include a tiny confidence score (how much of regression is due to model vs prompt drift).
sam: metrics we must ship with: p50/p95 latency, tokens/op, cost_per_1k_tokens, quality_scores (eval set), estimated cost delta if quantized. need format for customers to validate.
olivia: launch criteria (proposed):
- recs: 80% of recs validated by internal bench vs ground truth within +/-10% for latency & cost;
- alerts: detect regressions seen in retrospective test (holdout) with >=90% precision;
- UX: exportable CSV + simple recommendations UI;
- privacy: no customer prompts leave our infra (work with PrivSec);
- docs: runbook + rollback guide.
jen: add SLOs: recommendation generation <= 24h for batch job, alert delivery <= 5m after eval job finishes, max false positive rate target 10% (first 3 months).
maya: flags: quant recs can change quality. must include eval harness per-cust and opt-out by default. also legal/reg issues for auto-quant in Private deployments.
kevin: implementation sketch:
- offline runner: ingest sample traces -> simulate batching & KV caching -> run candidate quant profiles (hnnsim) -> score cost/latency/quality tradeoffs
- API: /optimize/recommendations?model=...&window=7d -> returns list
- alerts: hook evaler: POST /alerts with payload {eval_id, diffs}
```json
{
  "eval_id": "e-123",
  "diffs": {"qa_accuracy": -0.04},
  "recommended_actions": ["re-run with fallback", "open-support-ticket"]
}
```
jen: ok. can we get an initial spike: infra sim + minimal UI component? who owns which?
olivia: owners: kevin (infra & sim), maya (alerts & eval integration), jen (UX & docs), sam (quality gating + metrics). PM will run weekly sync until MVP.
product-bot: Created ticket OPT-422: "Optimize guidance - alerting plumbing" and OPT-423: "Offline recs runner"
kevin: timeline ask: spike (2w) -> alpha (4w) -> beta with 1 pilot customer (6w) -> GA after pilot feedback (4w). total ~16w.
maya: customer pilot asks: per-cust eval harness, SLA for alert triage, opt-out toggles, and clear QA rollback.
olivia: next steps: 1) spike plan posted in doc: https://redwood.internal/docs/optimize-autorec-spike (draft by friday); 2) create pilot checklist; 3) schedule pilot with FinPlatform (they gave greenlight to be first pilot).
sam: fine. I'll draft the metric schema and a small baseline eval set we can run against pilot traffic.
jen: I'll mock a UI table and export CSV flow.
kevin: assigning OPT-423 to me. starting spike tomorrow.
olivia: thanks all. we'll review spike outcomes next Wed. :rocket:
